mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over the last six months indicates strong economic demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances with positive GDP growth, or GDP growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 3-year rolling window (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% over the last two months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows and corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and housing market activity boost corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances with positive signals from both HOUST and RSAFS, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances with positive signals from both UNRATE and PAYEMS, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index over the last two months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a robust demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and confidence improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances with positive signals from both RSAFS and UNRATE, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
